decision.trend: The trend in the research is to develop high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with improved strength and ductility. Various processing techniques such as vacuum induction melting, directional solidification, and laser powder bed fusion have been used to produce HEAs with unique microstructures. The addition of elements such as hafnium, molybdenum, and tantalum has been shown to enhance the mechanical properties of HEAs. The use of computational screening and machine learning models has also been explored to discover new HEAs with optimized properties.
decision.unsolved: One of the remaining challenges is to overcome the traditional trade-off between strength and ductility in HEAs. While some studies have reported improved strength and ductility, others have found that the addition of certain elements can lead to a decrease in ductility. Further research is needed to understand the relationships between composition, processing, and microstructure on the mechanical properties of HEAs.
decision.why: The next step would be to develop a machine learning model that can predict the mechanical properties of HEAs based on their composition and processing conditions. This would allow for the rapid screening of new HEA compositions and processing techniques, and could potentially lead to the discovery of new HEAs with optimized strength and ductility.
